newsitem.title: USA: Florida Progress writes off coal assets.
newsitem.headline: Florida Progress writes off coal assets.

text.p: Florida Progress Corp said it took a fourth quarter charge of $25.2 million to reflect the continuation of depressed market conditions for Central Appalachian low-sulphur coal.
The after-tax charge, equal to $0.26 per share, was taken by Electric Fuels Corp, the company's transportation and energy subsidiary to provide for losses on coal properties.
Florida Progress said 1996 earnings from continuing operations, including the coal write off, rose to $250.7 million, or $2.59 per share, from $238.9 million, or $2.50 a share, in 1995.

The company said Electric Fuels had earnings of $27.1 million before the charge, up 12.9 percent over 1995 earnings of $24 million. The increase is primarily attributable to an increase in tonnage handled in 1996 by its marine and terminaling services operations.

Florida Power, the company's largest subsidiary, earned $232.6 million, or $2.40 per share, on revenues of $2.4 billion for the year, compared to earnings of $217.3 million, or $2.27 per share, on revenues of $2.3 billion in 1995.

Residential customer growth of about two percent last year was the primary reason for Florida Power's 2.9 percent increase in retail energy sales over 1995. Contributing to the increase was higher usage among commercial and industrial customers.
Florida Progress sold its 80 percent share of Advanced Separation Technologies Inc for $56 million and realized an after-tax gain of $23.5 million, or $0.24 per share.

On December 18, Florida Progress noted, it completed the divestiture of Echelon International Corp, formerly Progress Credit Corp. As part of the transaction, Florida Progress recorded a $26.3 million after-tax charge to earnings for the write-down certain Echelon assets and transaction costs associated with the divestiture.
This charge was excluded from earnings from discontinued operations, it noted. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
